text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's Interior ministry said it had launched a search for the deputy executive director of the state gas monopolist Bulgargas Penko Dimitrov who had been missing since late Wednesday.

-- Bulgaria's biggest business conglomerate Multigroup will not suspend its business in the country, company president Iliya Pavlov said after a powerful bomb apprantly aimed at him wrecked his car on a mountain road outside Sofia on Tuesday.
-- There are signs that shady economic structures in Bulgaria are going to fight back following a campaign by the ministry to fight organised crime, Interior Minister Bogomil Bonev said.
-- Bulgarians spend nearly two thirds of their income on food, a survey carried out by the National Statistics Institute showed. @
-- Bulgaria's cabinet decided to impose a 15 percent grain export tax until the end of the year to offset further grain shortages, Prime Minister Ivan Kostov said.
-- Bulgaria's armed forces new chief of staff General Miho Mihov said he has ordered an inspection of all armed forces warehouses as a part of his bid to fight corruption in the army.
-- Salaries of state employees will rise by 25 percent in October, Social Policy minister Ivan Neikov said. @

-- The Bulgarian state railways will introduce special prices from July 1 to attract tourists during the summer. The new prices are expected to be 11.5 percent lower than the current ones, the company said. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 91188
